profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, who had previously built companies acquired by IXC Communications. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company opened what it described as the largest data center in Texas in Carrollton in 2012, the anchor of the Dallas Fort Worth cluster that this registry row is part of, alongside CyrusOne buildings in nearby Allen, Lewisville, and Collin County. CyrusOne also operates a substantial San Antonio campus and an Austin facility, both long-running Texas markets for the company, though no specific acquisition or opening story for San Antonio or Austin individually was located in available sourcing this session. The company was acquired by ABRY Partners in 2007, purchased by Cincinnati Bell for 525 million dollars in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
This Carrollton campus publishes 45 MW of IT capacity across 600,000 square feet of technical space. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this translates to roughly 1,100 racks. The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 compliance, qualifying it for regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and government sectors.

The campus ranks third by published megawattage in Texas, behind only two other disclosed facilities in a state listing 133 mapped data centers but disclosing power figures for just 18 of them. Its 45 MW represents 9.6 percent of Texas's 468 MW of published capacity. The site is part of a Dallas-Fort Worth cluster that CyrusOne has operated since 2012, when this building was described as the largest data center in the state at opening.

The facility's capacity is moderate by current AI standards but substantial for the general-purpose enterprise market it is published to serve. Whether this campus matters to AI depends on whether its current tenant mix includes machine learning workloads and whether the operator has published expansion plans, neither of which is disclosed. The grid constraint on further growth at this address is not published.
